reference_title: Comprehensive Analysis of the Naturally Processed Peptide Repertoire: Differences between HLA-A and B in the Immunopeptidome.
antigen_processing_comments: Natural ligands of HLA class I molecules were eluted from four different B lymphoblastoid cell-lines (BLCL) in both steady state (uninfected) and following in vitro infection with measles virus. MHC-bound peptides were isolated using the HLA class I specific monoclonal antibody W6/32. pHLA complexes were eluted with 10% acetic acid and peptides were collected. Peptide analyses of the fractions were performed on a nanoscale LC-MS system. Class I allele assignments were made using NetMHC-3.2.
assay_comments: Compared to the total of 5,767 unique self-peptides eluted from the four BLCL in steady state (uninfected), only 4,112 unique self-peptides were found after MV infection. MV infection thus resulted in a 28.7% decrease in the number of unique peptides derived from self-proteins. The observed decrease was irrespective of the presenting HLA molecule (infected vs uninfected, p = 0.0007).

reference_title: The human leukocyte antigen-presented ligandome of B lymphocytes.
antigen_processing_comments: HLA-I peptidomes were eluted from EBV-transformed B lymphoblastoid cell lines, B-LCL-JYpp65 and B-LCL-HHC. After lysis, HLA-I molecules were immunoaffinity purified from lysate with the W6/32 antibody covalently bound to Protein-A Sepharose beads. Peptides were eluted from HLA using isoelectric focusing (IEF) separations, an OFFGEL Agilent 3100 fractionator followed by two chromatographic separation techniques, strong cation exchange chromatography (SCX) and RP-C18 chromatography. The dissolved fractions were analyzed via on-line nano-HPLC-MS and spectra were matched to IPI human database with Mascot. Scaffold software, version 3, was subsequently used to process the Mascot output.
